title: Reserve-throughput-zones and graceful-degradation protocol for dedicated fleets
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Dedicated GPU pools face unpredictable tenant-level bursts that either lead to tail latency spikes or aggressive global shedding which harms paying customers. Current admission logic is strictly first-come-first-serve with coarse priority bands; we lack per-customer baseline reservations and a predictable, observable degradation path when capacity is constrained.

Proposal: Implement Reserve Throughput Zones (RTZ) — a lightweight admission layer that allocates a guaranteed baseline throughput per tenant (or routing zone) and coordinates a shared overflow pool for bursts. Replace hard global shedding with a multi-phase graceful-degradation protocol that: 1) applies progressive request degradation (non-blocking to blocking), 2) routes excess low-priority traffic to fallback lanes (cheaper model variants / regional replicas / queued retry), and 3) emits deterministic retry-after semantics and error codes.

Key components: RTZ config model, per-tenant token lease with reclaim timers, shared overflow pool with leak-rate controls, elastic bounded queue with priority windows, degradation policy engine (phases + actions), autoscaler hooks (scale-up signals based on RTZ deficits), and observability dashboards + SLO checks.

Goals: predictably honor committed throughput for paying customers, reduce noisy global shedding, and provide clear HTTP-level signals so clients can implement backoff and fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and merged in /docs (architecture + config semantics)
Admission module implemented and covered by unit tests with >= 85% branch coverage
End-to-end perf tests show baseline throughput guarantees met for 95% of tenants under mixed load (metrics: guaranteed_tokens/sec delivered >= target, 95th latency < SLO)
Overflow pool yields burst capacity without exceeding fleet-wide token burn budget; test vectors show controlled degradation instead of all-or-nothing shedding
Canary rollout on one dedicated fleet for 2 weeks with automated rollback criteria defined
Dashboards with per-tenant reservation utilization, overflow consumption, queue depth, degradation phase, and SLO alerts created
Client-facing error codes and Retry-After headers documented and validated with SDK team
implementation_plan: Draft RTZ config schema and validation rules (owner: Lars)
Implement token-lease manager (in admission-controller package) with per-tenant counters and reclaim TTL
Create shared overflow pool with configurable leak rate and max-burst ceiling
Build elastic bounded queue that supports priority windows and max-wait SLA enforcement
Develop degradation policy engine with three phases: gentle (score/response truncation), moderate (rate-limit non-essential endpoints), severe (reject non-SLA traffic with Retry-After)
Expose hooks to autoscaler: deficit metric and burn-rate forecast
Add telemetry: reservation_granted, reservation_denied, overflow_used, queue_wait_ms, degradation_phase
Write e2e test scenarios covering steady load, correlated bursts, tenant noisy-neighbor, and autoscale reactions
Iterate on SDK guidance for retry semantics and best-effort fallbacks
Canary rollout with feature flag, monitor, then full fleet roll when metrics stable

qa_notes: Test scenario A: single tenant baseline under 80% load, verify 95th latency within SLO for baseline tokens
Test scenario B: burst test with 50x spike from one tenant for 30s; verify overflow pool absorbs expected burst and other tenants degrade gracefully
Test scenario C: autoscaler integration - simulate sustained deficit and confirm scale-up signal emitted within 30s
Failure mode: simulate overflow exhaustion and confirm correct Retry-After header and 429 semantics for non-SLA traffic
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged canary: enable RTZ on one small dedicated fleet (5% traffic) for 72h
Monitor: per-tenant guaranteed throughput hit-rate, queue depth, overflow burn, error-rate (429), tail latency
Stage 2: 25% fleets for 7d if metrics stable and no regressions
Full roll: remaining fleets with gradual ramp over 48h and automatic rollback on breach of rollback criteria
Rollback criteria: >1% of paying tenants lose >30% of committed throughput for >5 minutes OR fleet-wide 95th latency regresses by >20%
